definition: Grossberg network is an artificial neural network introduced by Stephen Grossberg.
details: It is a self organizing, competitive network based on continuous time. Grossberg, a neuroscientist and a biomedical engineer, designed this network based on the human visual system.

explainer.lead: The Grossberg network is an artificial neural network designed by Stephen Grossberg, using competition and continuous change over time to organize its activity. Its inspiration from the human visual system makes it an example of neural-network design informed by neuroscience.

tiers.eli5: It is a computer network modelled on how the eye and brain compete to make sense of what we see.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat it as a continuous-time, competitive self-organizing network rooted in vision modelling; a pitfall is assuming it behaves like modern feedforward networks.
tiers.paperLevel: A self-organizing, competitive artificial neural network operating in continuous time, designed by Grossberg from the human visual system. Known limits: the given facts do not specify learning rules, stability guarantees or performance bounds.

explainer.example: If several parts of the network respond to the same visual input, their activity continues to evolve while competition shapes which response becomes organized.

components.name: Continuous-time dynamics
components.detail: Network activity changes continuously over time rather than being defined only by discrete feed-forward passes.

components.name: Competitive interaction
components.detail: Competition within the network shapes its activity.

components.name: Self-organization
components.detail: The network develops organized behavior through its own dynamics.

flow: Network activity evolves continuously over time.
The dynamics produce a self-organized response.
explainer.origin: Stephen Grossberg, a neuroscientist and biomedical engineer, introduced the network and based its design on the human visual system.
explainer.whyItMatters: It connects continuous-time, competitive neural computation with a design motivation drawn from biological vision.
